summary: This program counts from 1 to 10 with a while loop, printing each number except the multiples of 3. It uses `continue` to jump straight back to the top of the loop when a number should be skipped.

lines.text: The counter starts at 1 because that is the first number we want to print.
The loop keeps running as long as the counter has not passed 10, so the last number considered is 10 itself.
The remainder operator `%` gives what is left over after dividing; a remainder of 0 means `i` divides evenly by 3 and should be skipped.
The counter must be advanced here, before skipping, or the loop would come back to the same multiple of 3 forever.
`continue` abandons the rest of this pass through the loop and jumps back to the `while` test, so the `print` below never runs for a multiple of 3.
This line is only reached for numbers that survived the skip test, which is exactly what we want on screen.
This is the normal increment for numbers that were printed, keeping the loop marching towards 10.
